lexemes.role: Yes/no question particle: put it at the start of a statement to turn it into a question (هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْجَزَرَ؟).

profile.feeling: Neutral question marker of written Arabic.

senses.def: yes/no question marker (placed before the statement)

synonyms.nuance: prefix question marker (أَتُحِبُّ …؟); required before a negation: أَلَيْسَ …؟

etymology.text: Univerbation of هَـ (ha-, an old interrogative, now أَ) + لـ (l-, an affirmative particle) (Wiktionary).

funFacts: Word order never changes in an Arabic question — هَلْ is all you add.
pitfalls: Before al- it takes a helping vowel: هَلِ الْبَصَلُ طَازَجٌ؟ (not هَلْ الْ…).
Not before a negation: “don’t you like …?” = أَلَا تُحِبُّ …؟ (with أَ), not *هَلْ لَا …
subtleties: Spoken Arabic often drops هَلْ and uses intonation alone; in writing it is expected.
